text: anya: sharing a quick mock — small multiples in the console, labels feel cramped when units switch to K/M. thoughts? simon: can you paste the mock? hard to picture. anya: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz — top row shows auto-scaling units (1.2M -> 1.2M), bottom row shows full numbers (1,234,567). also added a smoothing toggle per chart. talia: +1 on the smoothing toggle, but we should default it off for accuracy-critical views. users will be surprised if values look 'too clean'. evan: agree. also worried about the axis label wrap on narrow panes — currently it truncates mid-word. can we try simple unit suffixes (K, M) with hover tooltip for exact value? simon: tooltip works but keyboard/screenreader folks need accessible text. proposal: visible label shows compact unit, add aria-label with full expanded string. anya: example tooltip + aria sample: ``` 1.23M ``` figma-bot: uploaded image 1718456799 (small-multiples-compact-labels.png) evan: on outliers — current mock dims outliers by reducing opacity. i think dimming hides important spikes. alternative: cap the y-axis with a subtle marker + "+" sign for overflow, and show full value in tooltip. talia: i like cap+marker — keeps trend readable without suppressing the spike entirely. what about a per-chart policy: "cap by percentile" vs "full scale"? simon: implement by default: cap at 99th percentile with an overflow marker. add a menu option: "Show raw max". microcopy: label it "Show extreme values"? feels scary. evan: maybe: "Include outliers" — clearer. anya: wording vote: everyone reacts with emoji. :thumbsup: for "Include outliers", :thumbsdown: for "Show extreme values", :thinking_face: for other ideas. simon: accessibility nit — markers need alt text: "value exceeds chart range: 12,345,678" and must be reachable by keyboard. talia: layout nit — legend should remain left-aligned in narrow panes instead of wrapping into a second line. compress legend items with ellipsis and show full metric name in tooltip. evan: performance note — adding per-chart smoothing toggle means we need to persist preference per dashboard. keep it in local storage first, then add api for saved views. anya: action items: 1) try cap-at-99th mock + overflow marker (design) 2) implement compact unit with aria-labels (dev) 3) default smoothing OFF, add per-chart toggle + localStorage (dev) 4) legend compress + tooltip for full names (design/dev) 5) copy: use "Include outliers" for toggle. simon: i'll take #2 and #3. anya + talia can iterate on the cap marker and legend compress. evan can add copy to the UI strings. anya: thanks — i'll upload updated frames by EOD. figma-bot: comment pinned by anya: "cap-at-99th frame is frames/3" anya: small followup — in the mock i made the overflow marker a tiny chevron. open to using a + badge with ARIA label instead. evan: +badge with aria-label wins for discoverability. talia: cool. quick QA checklist for accessibility: keyboard focus on marker, screenreader announces "value exceeds chart range: 12,345,678", tooltip contains exact value, legend items reachable via keyboard and have aria-labels. simon: cheers. i'll start a PR for aria-label pattern and localStorage toggle. anya: thanks team :heart: "
